get.description: Get account wallet list

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Maximum number of items per page

parameters.name: filter
parameters.example: product_name eq 'SaaS Consumption-Licensing' or name contains ('product_usage','telco_usage')
parameters.description:
Filter wallets according to the specified filter expression.

Currently you can filter by the following attributes:
* `name` - Filter by wallet name.  E.g. `name eq 'product_usage'`.
* `product_name` - Filter by product name. E.g. `product_name eq 'SaaS Consumption-Licensing'`.
Supported comparison operators:
* `contains` - Match if any value is within the list, i.e. evaluates to true if any value of the contains operand matches the value in the database. E.g. `contains(product_name, 'standard')`.
* `eq` - Exact match, i.e. only evaluates to true if both operands have the same value. E.g. `name eq 'saas_licenses'`.
Supported logical operators:
* `and` - AND logical operator. E.g. `name eq 'saas_licenses' and product_name eq 'Talkdesk Fax'`.
* `or` - OR logical operator. E.g. `name eq 'saas_licenses' or product_name eq 'Talkdesk Fax'`.
* `not` - NOT logical operator. E.g. `not product_name eq 'product_usage'`.
Supported precedence operators:
* `(` and `)` - Parentheses precedence operator. You can force some expressions to be evaluated first than another by enclosing them into parentheses E.g. `(name eq 'saas_licenses' and product_name eq 'Talkdesk Fax') or name eq 'guardian'` is different than `name eq 'saas_licenses'
  and (product_name eq 'Talkdesk Fax' or name eq 'guardian')`.
Values must have single quotes marks e.g.: `name eq 'guardian'`

Examples
* `filter=product_name eq 'Saas Licenses' and (name eq 'saas_licenses' and contains(product_name, 'digital')` - Retrieve the wallets that have product_name 'Saas Licenses' and thatname is 'saas_licenses' or product_name contains the string 'digital' within.
* `filter=name eq 'ai_premium_batch' or contains(product_name, 'realtime') - Retrieves the wallets that have name 'ai_premium_batch' or that product_name contains the string 'realtime' within.

parameters.name: order_by
parameters.description:
Sorts by the indicated field in the specified direction, ascending or descending. The expression format may contain the suffix asc or desc separated from the property name with a colon in between.
Examples:
  • name:desc
More information here

post.description:
Assigns multiple ring groups to multiple agents. Some relevant caveats about the operation:
* The operation is idempotent and it returns successfully even if some users already have some of the ring
  groups (and for those cases the operation is a noop).

* As ring groups aren't really a resource on our domain, assigning a "non-existent" ring group to an agent has the
  side-effect of "creating" the ring group (e.g. the account ring groups endpoint will start listing it).

* The operation is non-transactional. This means that in case of an error the operation can be partially applied,
  even if a error status code is returned.

parameters.description:
Allows filtering by using comparison and logical operators.

  • To search parts of a string within a field of type string then the contains operator should be used.
    The syntax is the following: contains(field, 'value')

    • Logical operators are and and or.
    When using multiple ANDs and ORs, you should use parentheses to explicitly define the logical operators evaluation order.
    (note: this is recommended because the usual precedence rules aren't supported due to an implementation detail).

    Examples:
    • (contains(user_id, 'agent1') or contains(user_id, 'agent2')) and active eq true
    • contains(user_id, 'agent1')
    More information here

The endpoint allows you to retrieve the accounts associated with a specific contact.
By providing the unique contact ID as a path parameter, this endpoint enables you to fetch the financial or membership accounts linked to the contact.

parameters.name: contact_id
parameters.description: The contact id

parameters.name: skip
parameters.description: The number of elements to skip in accounts collection

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The maximum number of elements in accounts collection

parameters.description: The interaction id

currency_code.description: Currency used in this account using ISO 4217 standard

iban.description: IBAN number associated to this account

swift_code.description: SWIFT code associated to this account

account_name.description: Name provided by the account owner (nickname)

parties.description: List of parties. A party is a person or company associated with the account.

items.description: Party identity information

role.description: Type of role associated with a party member

custom_role.description: Account's customized party by bank client

transfer_permission.description: Indicates if the party has permission to transfer funds

balance.description: Account's booked balance. For loans this field will be equal to "Current Principal Balance"

custom_type.description: Account's customized type by bank client

custom_status.description: Account's customized status by bank client

custom_fields.description: Custom fields list. It allows the core the retrieve custom data for each FSI account.

previous_year_taxes_paid.description: One value expected with the sum of all year taxes paid

monthly_escrow_payment.description: Monthly escrow payment (detail amount of monthly_loan_payment)

account_routing_number.description: The MICR routing number consists of 9 digits (XXXXYYYYC) where XXXX is Federal Reserve Routing Symbol, YYYY is ABA Institution Identifier, and C is the check digit.

transfer_authorization.description: Transfer Authorization. INQUIRY means transfers and withdrawals not allowed; TRANSFERS means allowed transfers depending on transferRules; TRANSFERS_AND_WITHDRAWALS means allowed transfers depending on transferRules, and withdrawals to be made from the account.

transfer_in.description: Active when the account has permission to receive money from other accounts.

transfer_out_own_accounts.description: Active when the account has permission to send money between own accounts.

transfer_out_others.description: Active when the account has permission to send money to other accounts of the same bank.

transfer_out_external.description: Active when the account has permission to send money to other accounts of a different bank.

transfer_out_international.description: Active when the account has permission to send money to international accounts.

withdrawals_by_check.description: Active then allows withdrawals from the account by check.

total.description: Total number of accounts in the collection

post.description:
Update the Talkdesk contact information fields with the information of the FSI member.
To get the Talkdesk contact it is required to provided one of the query parameters: contact_id or phone_number.
When is provided the contact_id the Talkdesk contact to update will be found by the contact_id.
When is provided the phone_number the Talkdesk contact to update will be found if only one match of the **phone number** exists in the contact Api.
The update process will only occur only if a Talkdesk contact is retrieved and exists one Fsi member with identifier equals to **member_id**.
The Talkdesk contact information that may be updated will be:
 - Name
 - Address
 - Email
 - Phone numbers

200.description: The object with both agent ID and encrypted session nonce

schema.description: Session retrieved containing the agent ID and the nonce RSA encrypted.

post.description:
It creates a session for a given the session_key in the format <AGENT_NONCE>::<ACCOUNT_ID>::<AGENT_ID>, where:
  - <AGENT_NONCE>: uid
  - <ACCOUNT_ID>: account ID
  - <AGENT_ID>: agent ID
The endpoint validates that both account ID and agent ID provided in sesseion_key match with account ID and agent ID extracted from JWT (aid and uid, respectively):
  - if yes, a RSA public-private key pair is generated and the nonce is saved encrypted with the public key, and returned the private_key, for later decode the nonce.
  - otherwise a Bad Request is thrown.

200.description: The object with the encrypted RSA private key

session_key.description: The session key has to be in the format <AGENT_NONCE>::<ACCOUNT_ID>::<AGENT_ID>

post.description: Add (or update) a list of locations, services or staffs directories from a CSV file.

parameters.name: directory_type
parameters.description: The directory type.

file.description:
The file containing the rows to be upload at service directory List table.
The file must be a text file with text/csv content format and the allowed columns are:
 * SERVICE_ID
   - identifier of the service, will generate a random one if it empty
 * SERVICE_NAME
   - The name of the service, Any given string. It can include special chars.
 * SERVICE_TYPE
   - The type of the service, Any given string. It can include special chars.
 * DURATION
   - The duration of the service. Typically the time duration, number, etc.
 * DESCRIPTION
   - The DESCRIPTION the service
 * VIRTUAL_LOCATION_URL
   - The virtual_location_url of the service
 * PRICE
   - The price of the service.
 * PHONE_NUMBER
   - The phone number of the service, format should phoneNumber1:phoneNumberName1|phoneNumber2:phoneNumberName2
 * TIMEZONE
   - The time zone of the service, according to IANA.
 * BUSINESS_MON
   - Monday business hours. Example: 10:00AM-01:00PM | 02:00PM-08PM
 * BUSINESS_TUE
   - Tuesday business hours. Example: 10:00AM-01:00PM | 02:00PM-08PM
 * BUSINESS_WED
   - Wednesday business hours. Example: 10:00AM-01:00PM | 02:00PM-08PM
 * BUSINESS_THU
   - Thursday business hours. Example: 10:00AM-01:00PM | 02:00PM-08PM
 * BUSINESS_FRI
   - Friday business hours. Example: 10:00AM-01:00PM | 02:00PM-08PM
 * BUSINESS_SAT
   - Saturday business hours. Example: 10:00AM-01:00PM | 02:00PM-08PM
 * BUSINESS_SUN
   - Sunday business hours. Example: 10:00AM-01:00PM | 02:00PM-08PM
 * LOCATIONS
   - The location external ids of the service
 * SPECIAL_DATES
   - The special dates of the service in JSON format. Example: [{"name":"special date","date":"2025-03-20","repeat_rule":"DOES_NOT_REPEATS","business_hours":[{"open_at":"00:03:00","close_at":"12:58:00"}],"notes":""}]

202.description: The file has bean accepted and will be processed async by a task.
